citation.authors: Stewart ML, Wilcox ML, Bell M, Buggia MA, Maki KC
citation.title: Type-4 Resistant Starch in Substitution for Available Carbohydrate Reduces Postprandial Glycemic Response and Hunger in Acute, Randomized, Double-Blind, Controlled Study

population.description: Thirty-five adults analysed for satiety, GI and palatability (Table 2, 'All Participants (n = 35)'; 12 men, 23 women; 36 randomised, 32 in the glucose and insulin analyses). Age '46.2 +/- 2.2' and BMI '26.1 +/- 0.5' are means with SEM (Table 2 footnote), so sd = SEM x sqrt(35): 2.2 x 5.916 = 13.015 for age and 0.5 x 5.916 = 2.958 for BMI, computed. No min or max printed; inclusion ages 18-74 and BMI 18.5-29.99 (Methods 2.2, Study Subjects) are enrolment criteria, not the observed range. Status healthy: the aim is stated for 'healthy adults' (Introduction, 'to characterize the postprandial blood glucose response in healthy adults'), and the cohort excluded fasting capillary glucose >= 5.55 mmol/L (Methods 2.2).

protocols.name: control_scone
protocols.description: Control scone (refined wheat flour, Table 1 control column: 328 kcal, 38.8 g available carbohydrate as printed, 16.0 g fat, 7.1 g protein, 4.0 g fibre, 14.8 g sugars, 5.0 g saturated fat) eaten within 10 min with 240 mL water. Fasted on the morning of the visit (Methods 2.1). Timing (Methods 2.1, 2.4): the baseline venous sample was drawn 15 min before the scone (t = -15 +/- 2 min), eating began at t = 0 and took up to 10 min, and the other samples are at t = 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 min from the onset. For the iAUC the paper counts the t = -15 sample as t = 0 ('the pre-consumption measurement at t = -15 min was counted as t = 0'; trapezoidal rule), so the first interval is 15 min wide. The arm copies that: minute 0 is both the fasting baseline and the scone (a meal at t_min 0, taken as instant), samples at minutes 15 to 180, so the model's trapezoid is the paper's own; the 15 fasting minutes between the baseline draw and the scone are not run. Fasting length and clock hour are not printed: a 10 h fast and an 08:00 start are assumed; the 24 h diet record is not printed, so the arm starts from the default fed day. Control arm only; the fibre scone (RS4) is left out.

findings.description: Venous plasma glucose, incremental area over 0 to 120 min after the control scone (baseline sample drawn 15 min before the scone, counted as t = 0 by the paper; trapezoid over its samples as the paper defines it; what happens under baseline is not stated), mean and SEM over 32 subjects

capillary blood glucose (meter readings): iAUC0–120, iAUC0–180 and Cmax (Table 3, capillary section; 139.14 ± 14.60, 171.88 ± 19.65, 7.49 ± 0.19) and the fasting capillary glucose at screening and at the visits (Table 2): the same people and minutes as the venous glucose entered, at a different level (about twice the venous iAUC), so two targets for one glucose in one arm would contradict each other; only the venous one is entered (as stewart-2017)
